**“How would you manage a retained placenta?”**

“I would assess the maternal condition, quantify bleeding and check uterine tone. I would call for senior obstetric assistance, obtain IV access and appropriate blood tests, particularly if there is significant bleeding. I would establish how long the third stage has lasted and whether active management was used. I would avoid forceful cord traction and assess risk factors for placenta accreta, particularly previous Caesarean section and placenta praevia. If the placenta remains undelivered beyond the accepted timeframe or there is significant bleeding, I would arrange removal under appropriate anaesthesia, usually in theatre, with preparation for haemorrhage. If the placenta does not separate easily and accreta is suspected, I would stop attempting forceful removal and escalate immediately for specialist management because of the risk of catastrophic haemorrhage.”
